items.stem: Complete the statement: A cost driver is …
options: the factor that causes the cost of an activity to be incurred
the total cost of a product
a fixed overhead absorption rate
the manager responsible for a department
items.answer: the factor that causes the cost of an activity to be incurred
items.markingKey: Driver = cause of cost (e.g. number of set-ups) [1].

items.stem: Explain why machine set-up costs are better charged on the number of set-ups than on machine hours.
items.answer: Set-up cost depends on how many times machines are set up (batches), not on how long they run; using machine hours would overcharge long-run products and undercharge small batch products.
items.markingKey: Cost caused by set-ups [1]; distortion with machine hours [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the steps in calculating overhead costs using ABC.
items.answer: Identify activities and their cost pools; identify the cost driver for each; calculate a cost driver rate (pool ÷ total driver volume); charge products by their use of each driver.
items.markingKey: Activities/pools [1]; drivers [1]; rates [1]; charge to products [1] [4]

items.stem: Nimbus plc has materials handling costs of $11,400 for the period. The cost driver is the number of material movements, which totals 760. Calculate the cost driver rate and the materials handling cost charged to a product that uses 228 movements.
items.answer: $15.00 per movement; $3,420
items.markingKey: Rate = $11,400 / 760 = $15.00 per movement [1]; product uses 228 → $3,420 [1]

items.stem: Horizon plc has machine set-ups costs of $5,760 for the period. The cost driver is the number of set-ups, which totals 320. Calculate the cost driver rate and the machine set-ups cost charged to a product that uses 32 set-ups.
items.answer: $18.00 per set-up; $576

items.stem: Complete the statement: A cost pool is …
options: a grouping of overhead costs relating to one activity
the budgeted profit
a fund of cash for paying overheads
the total of direct costs
items.answer: a grouping of overhead costs relating to one activity
items.markingKey: Cost pool: costs of an activity collected together [1].

items.stem: Tamarind Ltd is introducing ABC. Suggest a suitable cost driver for each of these cost pools and explain one choice: (i) machine set-ups; (ii) quality inspection; (iii) materials handling.
items.answer: (i) number of set-ups; (ii) number of inspections; (iii) number of material movements. E.g. machine set-ups costs rise with the number of set-ups, so this reflects how products cause the cost.
items.markingKey: (i) number of set-ups [1]; (ii) number of inspections [1]; (iii) number of material movements [1]; explanation of cause-and-effect [1] [4]

items.stem: Delta Ltd is introducing ABC. Suggest a suitable cost driver for each of these cost pools and explain one choice: (i) materials handling; (ii) quality inspection; (iii) machine maintenance.

items.stem: Complete the statement: The overhead cost per unit under ABC for a product is found by …
options: adding the overheads charged from each cost pool and dividing by the units produced
multiplying labour hours by a single rate
dividing total overheads by total units
dividing selling price by units
items.answer: adding the overheads charged from each cost pool and dividing by the units produced
items.markingKey: Σ(driver usage × rate) / units [1].

items.stem: Explain why ABC may give a more accurate product cost than a single blanket overhead rate.
items.answer: It recognises that different products use activities in different proportions and charges overheads according to the causes, rather than assuming all overheads vary with labour or machine hours.
items.markingKey: Multiple drivers reflect causes [1]; avoids cross-subsidy [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain how ABC information could be used in pricing decisions.
items.answer: More accurate full costs show which products are under-priced (making losses) or over-priced; prices can be set to cover the true cost plus margin.
items.markingKey: Accurate cost base [1]; identify mis-priced products [1] [2]

items.markingKey: Blanket/departmental OAR on volume-related basis [1].

items.stem: Explain two disadvantages of introducing activity-based costing.
items.answer: High cost of collecting data on activities and drivers; choosing drivers can be subjective; some costs (e.g. rent) have no clear driver; staff may resist change.
items.markingKey: Two disadvantages [1 each] + explanation [1 each] [4]

items.stem: Explain why ABC is more relevant in modern manufacturing than traditional absorption costing.
items.answer: Overheads now form a large proportion of cost and are driven by complexity (set-ups, orders, inspections) rather than labour hours, which are a small part of cost in automated factories.
items.markingKey: Overheads large/support activities [1]; labour no longer a good basis [1] [2]

items.stem: The production manager of Kestrel plc says: "Our low-volume product Deluxe looks very profitable under absorption costing, so we should make more of it." The product is made in many small batches and needs frequent inspections. Explain why ABC might change this conclusion.
items.answer: Deluxe causes many set-ups and inspections; absorption costing spreads these over labour hours, under-costing Deluxe and over-costing Standard. ABC may show Deluxe is much less profitable or loss-making.
items.markingKey: Batch-level costs not linked to labour hours [1]; under-costing of low-volume product [1]; possible change in decision [1] [3]

Condor Ltd sets prices at full cost plus 25% using a single direct labour hour overhead rate. Products Basic (12,000 units) and Elite (3,000 units) share overheads in these cost pools: engineering changes $15,000 (driver: number of design changes; Basic 30, Elite 70); quality inspection $22,500 (driver: number of inspections; Basic 15, Elite 60); materials handling $10,000 (driver: number of material movements; Basic 10, Elite 40). Labour hours per unit: Basic 2, Elite 3. Direct costs per unit: Basic $40, Elite $45. Current prices: Basic $54, Elite $62. (a) Calculate the overhead cost per unit of each product using the labour hour rate. (b) Calculate the profit or loss per unit of each product at current prices using ABC costs.
items.answer: (a) Basic $2.88; Elite $4.32 (b) Basic $13.08; Elite $4.83

items.stem: The production manager of Tamarind Ltd says: "Our low-volume product Beta looks very profitable under absorption costing, so we should make more of it." The product is made in many small batches and needs frequent inspections. Explain why ABC might change this conclusion.
items.answer: Beta causes many set-ups and inspections; absorption costing spreads these over labour hours, under-costing Beta and over-costing Alpha. ABC may show Beta is much less profitable or loss-making.
items.markingKey: Batch-level costs not linked to labour hours [1]; under-costing of low-volume product [1]; possible change in decision [1] [3]

items.stem: Odyssey plc: Products Mono (40,000 units) and Duo (5,000 units) share overheads in these cost pools: materials handling $160,000 (driver: number of material movements; Mono 100, Duo 300); quality inspection $80,000 (driver: number of inspections; Mono 40, Duo 160). Each unit of Mono needs 0.5 direct labour hours and each unit of Duo needs 2. Calculate the overhead cost per unit of each product using (a) a single direct labour hour rate and (b) ABC, and comment on the difference.
items.answer: (a) OAR $8.00 per hour: Mono $4.00, Duo $16.00 (b) Mono $1.40, Duo $36.80. Duo is undercosted under the traditional method.
items.markingKey: (a) total overheads $240,000 / 30,000 hours = $8.00 [1]; per unit $4.00, $16.00 [1] (b) ABC rates and totals [2]; per unit $1.40, $36.80 [1]; comment: Duo consumes more activities than its labour hours suggest [1]

items.stem: Lynx Ltd sets prices at full cost plus 25% using a single direct labour hour overhead rate. Products Alpha (5,000 units) and Beta (500 units) share overheads in these cost pools: machine maintenance $21,000 (driver: machine hours; Alpha 2,500, Beta 1,000); machine set-ups $10,000 (driver: number of set-ups; Alpha 25, Beta 75); quality inspection $40,000 (driver: number of inspections; Alpha 100, Beta 300). (a) Calculate the overhead cost per unit of each product using the labour hour rate. (b) Calculate the profit or loss per unit of each product at current prices using ABC costs.
Complete the statement: The most appropriate cost driver for quality inspection costs is …
options: the number of inspections
the value of materials used
the number of employees
machine hours
items.answer: the number of inspections
items.markingKey: Inspection cost driven by inspections [1].

items.stem: Galaxy Ltd is introducing ABC. Suggest a suitable cost driver for each of these cost pools and explain one choice: (i) customer service; (ii) despatch; (iii) machine set-ups.
items.answer: (i) number of customer orders; (ii) number of despatches; (iii) number of set-ups. E.g. customer service costs rise with the number of customer orders, so this reflects how products cause the cost.
items.markingKey: (i) number of customer orders [1]; (ii) number of despatches [1]; (iii) number of set-ups [1]; explanation of cause-and-effect [1] [4]

items.stem: Equinox plc has customer service costs of $51,300 for the period. The cost driver is the number of customer orders, which totals 1,710. Calculate the cost driver rate and the customer service cost charged to a product that uses 171 customer orders.
items.answer: $30.00 per customer order; $5,130
items.markingKey: Rate = $51,300 / 1,710 = $30.00 per customer order [1]; product uses 171 → $5,130 [1]

items.stem: Meridian Ltd has engineering changes costs of $25,020 for the period. The cost driver is the number of design changes, which totals 1,390. Calculate the cost driver rate and the engineering changes cost charged to a product that uses 417 design changes.

items.stem: Monarch plc sets prices at full cost plus 25% using a single direct labour hour overhead rate. Products Lite (12,000 units) and Pro (3,000 units) share overheads in these cost pools: machine maintenance $60,000 (driver: machine hours; Lite 6,000, Pro 9,000); engineering changes $7,500 (driver: number of design changes; Lite 10, Pro 40); materials handling $150,000 (driver: number of material movements; Lite 40, Pro 160). Labour hours per unit: Lite 1, Pro 2. Direct costs per unit: Lite $20, Pro $25. Current prices: Lite $40, Pro $61. (a) Calculate the overhead cost per unit of each product using the labour hour rate. (b) Advise the directors whether they should adopt ABC for pricing.
items.answer: (a) Lite $12.08; Pro $24.17 (b) ABC reveals cross-subsidy between products; adopt if benefits of better pricing exceed the cost of the system; consider competitors' prices and market reaction.
items.markingKey: (a) OAR $217,500/18,000 = $12.08 [1]; per unit [1] [2] (b) Uses results [2]; cost/benefit of ABC [1]; recommendation [1] [4]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: The overhead cost per unit under ABC for a product is found by … (b) Complete the statement: Under ABC, a low-volume product made in many small batches is likely to have …
items.answer: (a) adding the overheads charged from each cost pool and dividing by the units produced (b) a higher overhead cost per unit than under absorption costing
items.markingKey: (a) Σ(driver usage × rate) / units [1]. (b) Batch-level costs spread over few units [1].

items.stem: Horizon plc makes 5,000 units of Mono and 500 units of Duo. Customer service costs of $40,000 are driven by the number of customer orders (Mono 25, Duo 75). A trainee charged $36,364 to Mono by sharing the cost in proportion to units produced. Explain the error and calculate the correct charge.
items.answer: Under ABC costs are charged by driver usage, not units. Rate = $400.00; Mono charge = 25 × $400.00 = $10,000.
items.markingKey: Units are not the driver [1]; rate $400.00 [1]; correct charge $10,000 [1] [3]

items.stem: Sunbird plc makes 40,000 units of Alpha and 5,000 units of Beta. Despatch costs of $16,000 are driven by the number of despatches (Alpha 40, Beta 160). A trainee charged $14,222 to Alpha by sharing the cost in proportion to units produced. Explain the error and calculate the correct charge.
items.answer: Under ABC costs are charged by driver usage, not units. Rate = $80.00; Alpha charge = 40 × $80.00 = $3,200.
items.markingKey: Units are not the driver [1]; rate $80.00 [1]; correct charge $3,200 [1] [3]
